clue.text: Smack soundly? I shall be in trouble after that, it's wrong

indicators.note: after that puts the next piece behind the one already built
soundly says the word for smack is only to be heard, so a different spelling with the same sound is used

parts.note: to smack someone lightly with the lips is to peck them

indicators.note: be in tells us the contracted I shall sits inside the word for trouble

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
I shall contracts to I'll

explanation.surface: Someone contemplates giving a loud smack, knowing they will be in trouble for misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' signals a spelling that is only heard alike, and 'be in' marks the container; 'after that' places the trouble part last.
explanation.definitionFit: A peccadillo is a small sin or minor offence, something done wrong.

clue.text: New form of clip-art about to be introduced in examination

indicators.note: to be introduced in says the word for about goes inside the rearranged letters
New form of says the letters of clip-art are rearranged into a fresh shape

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A test in which pupils must redesign a piece of clip-art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New form of' marks the anagram of clip-art, and 'to be introduced in' sets circa's abbreviation inside it, near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical is an examination testing hands-on skills rather than written knowledge.

clue.text: Such literary works are genuine, as a rule

definitions.meaning: the authentic body of writings accepted as truly by an author
a principle or law, as in church law

explanation.definitionFit: Canon means both the accepted authentic works of a writer and a general rule or principle.

clue.text: French name for German town gets a man in exile all confused

indicators.note: in places the fellow inside the jumbled letters
confused says the letters of exile all are mixed up

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man living abroad in exile is thoroughly bewildered by the names of foreign towns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' looks like part of a phrase but is the synonym; 'confused' marks the anagram and 'in' puts the fellow in its middle. Aachen was Charlemagne's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Aix-la-Chapelle is the French name for Aachen, a German city near the Belgian border.

clue.text: Slight cut in blood sugar regulated by this

indicators.note: cut says the final letter is chopped from the word for slight

parts.note: a slight is an insult

explanation.surface: A small cut affects the level of sugar in someone's blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' looks like an adjective but is the noun meaning an affront; 'cut' docks the T of INSULT.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is the hormone that controls the level of glucose in the blood.

clue.text: Temporary arrangements involving horse riding — girl's put out

indicators.note: put out says the girl word is stretched open to take the other pieces inside

parts.note: a lass is a girl; the 's stands for is
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse
up means riding, as a jockey is up on a horse

explanation.surface: A girl is upset that her horse-riding plans have been thrown together at short notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is drug slang for heroin, and a jockey is 'up' when mounted; 'put out' has the girl stretched open around them, with 'involving' a mere link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lash-ups are makeshift improvised arrangements, cobbled together for the time being.

clue.text: Keen to have French Revolution artist guillotined

indicators.note: guillotined means beheaded, so the first letter of the artist's name is chopped off

parts.note: Jacques-Louis David was the painter of the French Revolution

explanation.surface: An eager painter of the Revolution ends up losing his head himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guillotined' takes the head, D, off DAVID; the surface is apt, since David lived through the Terror.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid is a synonym of keen: both describe eager enthusiasm.

clue.text: After half portion of curry,'e forks out for wine

indicators.note: After places the curry piece before the rest
half portion of keeps only the first four letters of the curry word

parts.note: vindaloo is a hot curry
'e is a dropped-aitch he, giving just E
to fork out is to pay, so he forks out becomes he pays

explanation.surface: After eating half his curry, a diner pays up for the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half portion of' docks ALOO from VINDALOO to leave VIND; 'e PAYS completes it, the apostrophe showing a dropped H.
explanation.definitionFit: Vin de pays is a French classification of country wine, a step above table wine.

clue.text: Woman is supporting debtor with nothing put away

indicators.note: supporting, in a down clue, means sitting beneath the piece above
put away says the nothing symbol is tucked inside the debtor abbreviation

parts.note: DR is the accounting abbreviation for debtor
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A woman backs a debtor who has squirrelled nothing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put away' marks the container, and 'supporting' works because in a down entry the supporting word sits underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Illegally seizes outbuildings

definitions.meaning: a state that ... territory takes it over without right
... are extra buildings attached to or near a main one

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means takes territory by force; the noun means added or subsidiary buildings.

clue.text: Dish with cashews passed round replacing first half of meal

indicators.note: replacing first half of says the opening three letters of the meal word are swapped out for the other piece

parts.note: dinner is a meal

indicators.note: passed round says the word for cashews is turned about, read backwards

parts.note: cashews are nuts

explanation.surface: A bowl of cashews is handed round in place of the starter at a dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' looks like food beside meal and cashews, but it is slang for a looker; 'passed round' and 'replacing first half of' do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish is slang for an attractive person, and a stunner is a strikingly good-looking one.

clue.text: Welsh play worked in Mold in new production by university

indicators.note: by means next to, so the university letter sits beside the rearranged letters
new production says the letters of the preceding words are staged in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A Welsh drama is staged afresh in the town of Mold, near a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the anagram fodder, not a link. Mold is a town in north Wales, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Under Milk Wood is Dylan Thomas's radio play set in a Welsh fishing village.

clue.text: Stretch of forest on Galapagos Islands

indicators.note: Stretch of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tract of woodland on the Galapagos Islands is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Pacific nation made up of many islands.

clue.text: Regularly clean posh new clothes? She could be on hand to help

definitions.text: She could be on hand to help

indicators.note: Regularly picks every other letter of the word clean, here its second and fourth

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class, posh usage
dress is clothing, attire

explanation.surface: Someone is advised to wash their smart new clothes routinely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes LA from cLeAn. The surface's cleaning of clothes is exactly what the woman defined does for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundress is a woman employed to wash clothes, a helper available to do the household washing.

clue.text: Pause for inspiration?

parts.note: read as stopping to wait for an idea, but inspiration here is literally drawing air into the lungs, so it means stopping to recover breathing

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stop briefly to recover after exertion, taking in air before continuing.

clue.text: In reversal of fortunes, become obese

definitions.meaning: a change from bad to good or the reverse
literally to grow rotund, to get fat

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a reversal; read literally as a verb phrase it means to get fat.

clue.text: Journalists organised stay inside country piles

indicators.note: inside places the rearranged letters within the journalists word

parts.note: hacks is slang for journalists

indicators.note: organised says the letters of stay are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Reporters arrange to stay at grand country houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' marks the anagram and 'inside' the container. 'country piles' suggests stately homes but means heaps of hay.
explanation.definitionFit: Haystacks are large heaps of hay found in the countryside.

clue.text: Writer's employed to recreate fictional character

indicators.note: to recreate says the letters of the preceding words are rebuilt into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An author is hired to bring a well-known fictional figure back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'Writer's' counts as a letter here. The detective was created by Dorothy L. Sayers, so the surface's hired writer recreating him is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Peter Wimsey is the aristocratic amateur detective of Dorothy L. Sayers's novels, a fictional character.

clue.text: High tension? With wild animal round about, you'll get even more tense

indicators.note: round about says the animal's name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a tiger is a wild animal
HT is the abbreviation for high tension in electrics

explanation.surface: With a tiger prowling nearby, already high tension rises further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round about' marks the big cat surrounding the electrical abbreviation; the opening question mark is part of the surface, not a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tighter is the comparative of tight, which can mean tense or taut.

clue.text: Feel giddy shortly after swallowing drinks and fall ill again

indicators.note: swallowing says the shortened word takes the drinks word inside it
shortly says the word for feeling giddy loses its last letter

parts.note: to reel is to feel giddy
laps means drinks, as a cat does milk

explanation.surface: Someone feels dizzy soon after downing drinks and is taken ill once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' docks a final letter and 'swallowing' marks the container; 'after' is only a link in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to suffer a return of illness after seeming recovery.

clue.text: Story book mislaid by girl who's given brief support?

indicators.note: mislaid says the abbreviation for book is lost from the story word

parts.note: a parable is a moral story
gal is an informal word for girl

explanation.surface: A girl has lost a storybook somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mislaid' drops B from PARABLE to leave PARALE. A 'brief' is a barrister's case, and the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A paralegal is a trained assistant who supports lawyers, so they help with a legal brief.

clue.text: Crush a foreign officer

parts.note: a pash is an infatuation, a schoolgirl crush

explanation.surface: Someone has a crush on an officer from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: PASH is dated British slang for a crush or infatuation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasha was a high-ranking Ottoman official or military commander.

clue.text: Not working, so finally seek a position

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word seek

parts.note: to put something is to position it

explanation.surface: Someone out of work is told to go and look for a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaput is slang for broken or no longer functioning.

clue.text: Tree and where it rarely grows, you say

indicators.note: you say signals the word is heard, not seen, so a same-sounding spelling goes in

parts.note: a plain is open, treeless land where trees seldom grow

explanation.surface: A tree is mentioned along with the kind of place it seldom grows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the tree; flat open grassland is typically treeless.
explanation.definitionFit: The plane is a tree with broad leaves and flaking bark, common in city streets.

clue.text: Trainee boss dispatched, not having succeeded

parts.note: a boss is a stud, a raised knob or ornament

indicators.note: not having says the abbreviation for succeeded is removed from the dispatched word

parts.note: sent means dispatched
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A trainee manager is sacked for failing to make the grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' looks like a manager but is the ornamental knob, STUD; 'not having' removes S from SENT to give ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A student is someone learning, a trainee in a subject or profession.

clue.text: Poetry would not be so unromantic

definitions.meaning: poetry, by definition, is not written in prose, the plain form of language

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means like prose, hence plain, dull and lacking poetic feeling.

clue.text: Area to mount opera

parts.note: Mount Ida is a mountain in Crete and in Turkey

explanation.surface: A space is set aside for staging an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Aida is Verdi's opera set in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Presumably Saturday never comes for such as Billy-No- Mates

definitions.text: Presumably Saturday never comes for such as Billy-No- Mates

parts.words: Presumably Saturday never comes for such as Billy-No- Mates
parts.note: read playfully, a week where Friday is endless never reaches Saturday; split the answer as the short form of Friday plus a word meaning without end

explanation.walkthrough: Billy-No-Mates is British slang for a person with no friends. The clue reads the answer as FRI plus ENDLESS: a Friday with no end, so Saturday never arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no companions at all is lonely and without any pals.
